source_title: Svante Janson (2014) Tibetan calendar mathematics Appendix D

notes.paraphrase: General day is integer local calendar JDN minus epoch JDN; E1927 uses 2424972. This is not Julian Date of an exact UTC instant.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Traditional general-day recovery from mean lunar count can be off by one; Janson documents a weekday check that repairs it.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Mercury uses 100×general day, Venus 10×, and Mars/Jupiter/Saturn 1× before applying planet-specific epoch offsets.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: E1927 source constants R=(8797,2247,687,4332,10766), offsets=(4639,301,157,3964,6286) for Mercury/Venus/Mars/Jupiter/Saturn, respectively.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Mean heliocentric longitude is particular_day/R modulo one full circle, normally rendered in mansion fractions and a planet-specific final radix.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: The planet-specific so-called birth-sign is a modeled aphelion/reference longitude, not the natal zodiac sign of a person.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Planetary mean solar longitude uses separate daily rate18382/6714405 and epoch1−458772/6714405 in E1927, rather than the tithi-ending mean Sun.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Janson notes the Tsurphu solar term can use the lunar-day mean Sun or another true-Sun variant; E1927 Phugpa constants do not define a Tsurphu planetary engine.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: For Mercury/Venus, slow mean is Sun and step index is heliocentric planet; for Mars/Jupiter/Saturn the assignments are reversed.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Slow correction is based on 12×(mean_slow−birthsign) and planet-specific Table12 values with antisymmetry and linear interpolation.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Traditional true slow longitude equals mean slow minus source table correction divided by 27×60, preserving circle periodicity.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Final correction uses 27 steps, planet-specific Table13 positive values at indices0–13, antisymmetry for the remaining half, and linear interpolation.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Traditional geocentric model longitude equals true slow plus fast step correction divided by 27×60; it is not an observed modern planetary longitude.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Rahu node period is 6900 lunar days=230 lunar months; this corresponds to about6792 calendar days, distinct from a 6900-solar-day period.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Rahu uses x=30n+D+30 rd0 lunar days, with rd0=187 at E1927 and 10 at E1987; the correct true-month count/calendar policy must be supplied.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

notes.paraphrase: Node Head longitude is (−x/6900) mod1 and Tail is Head+1/2 mod1; the node index is a mathematical category, not a physical planet.
notes.source_status: Modern mathematical exposition based partly on Henning/Schuh; not independent original Tibetan witness

scope: Appendix D.1–D.6, Table11–13, exact mathematical source rules; no physical ephemeris validation
